## Summary

Research confidence is **Moderate**. Some of this break's ideal conditions are confirmed by sources; others rest on limited evidence. It is the class the app computes from the evidence (how well the break's ideal conditions are documented), not a forecast and not a probability.

Main gaps:

- Sources disagree about the best tide.
- Limited information is available about the swell period this break needs.

| Swell period | Low | No sources found. |

Research notes (research_evidence.json):

> Re-read 4 of 6 current sources; surfertoday.com and surfer.com returned 403 and are kept unchanged. New readable sources: USGS image description (official) with the first bathymetry evidence (relict submerged boulder delta 1,500 m offshore refracts waves), Surf Atlas (2024), and Stab (2023, storm debris changed the point). Wind: three readable statements support the profile's 20 deg offshore: surf-forecast.com NE (45), Surf Atlas NE for most of the wave (45), and N-NE at the Cove (22). Surf Atlas says Indicator prefers a more easterly offshore. WannaSurf lists NW as the good wind, which conflicts with all of these (value null). Direction: W-NW is consistent across Wikipedia, surf-forecast.com, WannaSurf and Surf Atlas. Note that surf-forecast.com says WNW in its description but 'a West swell' in its best-conditions line. Tide conflict: Wikipedia (low) and Surf Atlas (low tide barrels) support low_to_mid; surf-forecast.com says all stages. Size: Surf Atlas says it maxes out at 13-15 ft, above the profile's 12 ft. Surfer Today's 4-8 ft and Surfer's 6 ft+ (web_search) remain unverified. Swell period: no number in any readable source. Surf Atlas only says locals wait for when 'the period is just right', and Stab mentions very long period swells as a regional forecast, so neither was recorded. Not recorded: Stormrider Ventura says W swells have the most power county-wide (not Rincon-specific), and an O'Reilly et al. 1999 PDF on Santa Barbara Channel swell sheltering (regional, not Rincon-specific; not read). Bathymetry is a cobble/boulder delta, so it changes after floods (Stab 2023).

## Ideal conditions

Directions are compass degrees the swell or wind comes FROM, ranges clockwise. Heights keep the scale each source states (breaking face, Hawaiian, swell or relative to the surfer); the app's sizes are breaking face heights in feet. Sources are numbered as in [Sources](#sources).

### Swell height

| Field | Research value | Status | Sources | App model setting |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Minimum suitable | — | not documented | — | `wave_height_min_ft` 3 ft (breaking face) |
| Ideal range | 4–8 ft [S8] · 6 ft or more [S9] (scale not stated) | conflicting | S8, S9 | no separate setting; working range 3–12 ft |
| Maximum suitable | 13–15 ft (scale not stated) | documented | S6 | `wave_height_max_ft` 12 ft (breaking face) |

Notes:

- **Minimum suitable**: No excerpt states a minimum working size; SurferToday's 4-8 ft is called ideal and SURFER's 6 ft plus is where it comes really alive (both search summaries, recorded under ideal_range).
- **Ideal range**: SurferToday says its ideal swell ranges from four to eight feet, while SURFER says it comes really alive in the six foot plus range (both search summaries, neither stating face or offshore height), so they disagree on whether sizes above 8 ft are better or worse.
  - S8 (SurferToday): “Its ideal swell is from the west and northwest, ranging from four to eight feet.”
  - S9 (SURFER Magazine): “the spot comes really comes alive in the six foot plus range, and that it works with north to north east wind”
- **Maximum suitable**: Surf Atlas speaks of Rincon pushing its max of 13-15 foot, without saying whether this is face or offshore height.
  - S6 (Surf Atlas): “When Rincon is pushing its max of 13-15 foot”

### Swell direction

| Field | Research value | Status | Sources | App model setting |

Notes:

- **Ideal bearing**: Wikipedia says best with swells mostly from the west and northwest, SurferToday (search summary) that its ideal swell is from the west and northwest, Surf Atlas that winter NW and direct W swells get it firing, and Surf-Forecast gives west-northwest (about 292.5 deg) as ideal.
  - S1 (Wikipedia): “It is best at low tide during the winter months when swells are coming mostly from the west and northwest.”
  - S2 (Surf-Forecast.com): “Most of the surf here comes from groundswells and the ideal swell direction is from the west northwest.”
  - S6 (Surf Atlas): “Winter NW swells and direct W swells march through a gap between the Channel Islands and Point Conception to get it firing”
  - S8 (SurferToday): “Its ideal swell is from the west and northwest, ranging from four to eight feet.”
- **Acceptable range**: WannaSurf lists NorthWest and West as the good swell directions; no source states a wider window, although Wikipedia and SURFER mention summer south swells for the Indicator lefts.
  - S3 (WannaSurf): “Good swell directionNorthWest, West”
- **Blocked directions**: No excerpt names swell directions that are blocked or shadowed by land or reefs.
- **Exposure**: Surf Atlas says winter NW and direct W swells march through a gap between the Channel Islands and Point Conception and that linking the sections needs the biggest swells of the year, usually from the direct west, while Surf-Forecast calls it a fairly exposed point break.
  - S6 (Surf Atlas): “Winter NW swells and direct W swells march through a gap between the Channel Islands and Point Conception to get it firing”
  - S2 (Surf-Forecast.com): “is a fairly exposed point break that has very consistent surf”
  - S6 (Surf Atlas): “It is VERY rare for that to happen, though, because it requires the biggest swells of the year, usually in the direct west channel”

  - S2 (Surf-Forecast.com): “Most of the surf here comes from groundswells and the ideal swell direction is from the west northwest.”
  - S1 (Wikipedia): “Indicator also produces some extremely fast left-breaking waves during the summer, when southerly swells are most prevalent.”

## Conflicting information

- **Swell height · ideal range**: SurferToday says its ideal swell ranges from four to eight feet, while SURFER says it comes really alive in the six foot plus range (both search summaries, neither stating face or offshore height), so they disagree on whether sizes above 8 ft are better or worse.
- **Wind · offshore**: Surf-Forecast says the best wind is from the northeast, Surf Atlas that NE is offshore for most of the wave (Indicator's offshore is more E) and that the Cove meets the N-NE Santa Ynez winds, and SURFER (search summary) that it works with north to northeast wind, while WannaSurf lists NorthWest as the good wind direction.
- **Tide · preferred stage**: Wikipedia says it is best at low tide and SurferToday (search summary) that all three breaks improve as the tide drops with tubes at low tide, while Surf-Forecast says good surf at all stages of the tide.
